narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the prose frame and introduces each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: Upright man of Hus, father of ten grown children, stricken and lamenting.

1.t: After this, Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day,

3.t: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said: A man child is conceived.

4.t: Let that day be turned into darkness, let not God regard it from above, and let not the light shine upon it.

5.t: Let darkness, and the shadow of death, cover it, let a mist overspread it, and let it be wrapped up in bitterness.

6.t: Let a darksome whirlwind seize upon that night, let it not be counted in the days of the year, nor numbered in the months.

7.t: Let that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise.

8.t: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to raise up a leviathan:

9.t: Let the stars be darkened with the mist thereof: let it expect light, and not see it, nor the rising of the dawning of the day:

10.t: Because it shut not up the doors of the womb that bore me, nor took away evils from my eyes.

11.t: Why did I not die in the womb? why did I not perish when I came out of the belly?

12.t: Why received upon the knees? why suckled at the breasts?

13.t: For now I should have been asleep and still, and should have rest in my sleep:

14.t: With kings and consuls of the earth, who build themselves solitudes:

15.t: Or with princes, that possess gold, and fill their houses with silver:

16.t: Or as a hidden untimely birth, I should not be; or as they that, being conceived, have not seen the light.

17.t: There the wicked cease from tumult, and there the wearied in strength are at rest.

18.t: And they sometime bound together without disquiet, have not heard the voice of the oppressor.

19.t: The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

20.t: Why is light given to him that is in misery, and life to them that are in bitterness of soul?

21.t: That look for death, and it cometh not, as they that dig for a treasure:

22.t: And they rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave?

23.t: To a man whose way is hidden, and God hath surrounded him with darkness?

24.t: Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring:

25.t: For the fear which I feared, hath come upon me: and that which I was afraid of, hath befallen me.

26.t: Have I not dissembled? have I not kept silence? have I not been quiet? and indignation is come upon me.
